publications.name: Stochastic dominance for claim spacings from heterogeneous insurance portfolios
publications.citation: Pu, T., Yong, Y., Zhang, J., & Zhang, Y. (2026). "Stochastic dominance for claim spacings from heterogeneous insurance portfolios." Statistical Theory and Related Fields. Advance online publication. https://doi.org/10.1080/24754269.2026.2733597
publications.summary: The difference between the largest and smallest claims, and the gap between the two smallest claims, reveal aspects of portfolio dispersion that aggregate losses can hide. This paper develops stochastic comparisons for these quantities in insurance portfolios whose policies differ in claim probabilities and severities. Its results explain how heterogeneity and dependence affect claim ranges and local claim gaps under explicit model conditions.

publications.name: Vulnerability-Conditional Systemic Risk Measures: Evidence from Cryptocurrency Markets
publications.citation: Pu, T., Wei, Y., & Zhang, Y. (2026). "Vulnerability-Conditional Systemic Risk Measures: Evidence from Cryptocurrency Markets." Risk Sciences. Advance online publication. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.risk.2026.100066
publications.summary: This paper studies an asset’s tail risk when at least one other market participant is in distress. It introduces a vulnerability-conditional expected-shortfall measure and distinguishes total conditional risk from absolute and relative spillover contributions. An application to five cryptocurrencies illustrates the measures and evaluates their calibration through backtesting.

publications.name: On multivariate contribution measures of systemic risk with applications in cryptocurrency market
publications.publisher: Probability in the Engineering and Informational Sciences
publications.citation: Wen, L., Li, J., Pu, T., & Zhang, Y. (2025). "On multivariate contribution measures of systemic risk with applications in cryptocurrency market." Probability in the Engineering and Informational Sciences, 39(4), 551-578.
publications.summary: This paper asks how to compare an asset’s relative exposure when several other assets are distressed together. It develops multivariate contribution ratios with different benchmarks and applies them to Bitcoin, Ethereum and Monero to distinguish relative spillovers from absolute loss levels.

publications.name: On joint marginal expected shortfall and associated contribution risk measures
publications.citation: Pu, T., Zhang, Y., & Zhang, Y. (2024). "On joint marginal expected shortfall and associated contribution risk measures." Quantitative Finance, 24(7), 889-908.
publications.summary: This paper examines the additional tail losses faced by a market when both it and another market are under stress. It develops joint marginal expected shortfall and corresponding absolute and relative contribution measures, with comparison results and an application to international stock indices.

publications.name: Generalized location-scale mixtures of elliptical distributions: Definitions and stochastic comparisons
publications.publisher: Communications in Statistics - Theory and Methods
publications.citation: Pu, T., Zhang, Y., & Yin, C. (2024). "Generalized location-scale mixtures of elliptical distributions: Definitions and stochastic comparisons." Communications in Statistics - Theory and Methods, 53(11), 3851-3875.
publications.summary: A common mixing construction brings several asymmetric extensions of elliptical models into one framework for comparing multivariate risks. The resulting parameter criteria yield comparisons for aggregate insurance losses and maximum claim amounts, as well as an extension of Slepian’s inequality and Gini-index results in low dimensions.

publications.name: An Identity for Expectations and Characteristic Function of Matrix Variate Skew-normal Distribution with Applications to Associated Stochastic Orderings
publications.citation: Pu, T., Balakrishnan, N., & Yin, C. (2023). "An Identity for Expectations and Characteristic Function of Matrix Variate Skew-normal Distribution with Applications to Associated Stochastic Orderings." Communications in Mathematics and Statistics, 11(3), 629-647.
publications.summary: The paper studies how changes in location, scale, and skewness affect stochastic comparisons of matrix-valued asymmetric risks. A characteristic-function formula and an expectation-difference identity connect model parameters to six orders describing size, variability, joint tail probabilities, and dependence.
